meta.authority: GEOX computes and contrasts (local Python runtime; geox-direct MCP unavailable this session). ARIF / arifOS adjudicates.
law: Surfaces are the stored objects; stages are derived intervals between surfaces.
Every age is model-scoped (PROJECT_2026, LEGACY_TB, LEGACY_RECAL). No silent averaging.
Biostratigraphy calibrates surfaces as age windows, it does not create surfaces.
No data is not nondeposition. Hiatus bodies are drawn only where wells or published charts show missing section.
Facies bodies are basin-scale synthesis, not measured thickness. Horizontal axis is domain position, not distance.
meta.convention_note: PROJECT_2026 ages (Unified GEOX table / Phase I) are TOP-of-stage ages; LEGACY_TB ages (A-R master penetration chart, Shell TB-cycle scheme) are BASE-of-stage ages. Both name the same physical surfaces: Top III = Base IVA = DRU; Top IVA = Base IVB = LIU; Top IVB = Base IVC = UIU; Top IVC = Base IVD = SRU; Top IVD = Base IVE = Horizon III; Top IVE = Base IVF = Horizon II; Top IVF = Base IVG = Horizon I.
v2_2_laws: Apparent K-Ar age is not automatically crystallisation, eruption or emplacement age.
Regional analogues increase plausibility but do not prove local plumbing continuity.
Present-day stress compatibility is a permissibility constraint, not age evidence.
AVO is an interface response, not a unique lithology or age classifier.
Never transform an open hypothesis into a canonical event merely to simplify rendering.

contradictions.finding: The 15.4-15.5 Ma legacy age is the old-timescale age of base NN5 (BKSA95 15.6). Re-dated with GTS2012 it becomes 14.91, so ~0.5 Ma of the 1.2 Ma gap is a calibration artefact. The residual 0.71 Ma is real: the project places DRU inside NN5, not at its base.
contradictions.test: No DRU pick in the pen chart has NN control (Deluar-1, Ketam-1, South Lokan-1 are EOD-only). Pull raw NN4/NN5 occurrences at these wells; if NN5 is present below the DRU pick, R (14.91) is falsified and P survives.

contradictions.finding: At Gajah Hitam-1, Tiga Papan-2 and Maligan-1 the SRU pick lies inside NN10 (GTS2012 window 8.29-9.53 Ma). Constant-rate interpolation inside the bracketed NN10 span gives 9.41 / 9.36 / 9.38 Ma, so the legacy 9.4 Ma fits best. Project 9.53 is the base-NN10 approximation and sits on the window edge: it would need zero NN10 below the pick, but 8.5-110 m are observed. It is ~0.15 Ma too old, which does not matter for mapping. '8.6 Ma' is the BKSA95 age of base NN11. The hypothesis 'SRU = base NN11' (8.29 Ma GTS2012) is rejected because NN10 overlies the pick at all three wells. Solisip-1 is the outlier: NN11 lies below its B.S IVD pick (window 5.59-8.29), so either that pick is a younger surface or SRU is diachronous toward N Sabah.
contradictions.test: Re-tie Solisip-1 B.S IVD on seismic; trace SRU terminations from Maligan-1 / Tiga Papan-2 to Solisip-1 along KL2. Add more NN10-bracketed SRU picks to test the 9.4 Ma estimate.

contradictions.finding: The joint window from Gajah Hitam-1, Rusa Timur-1, Glayzer-3 and Solisip-1 is 9.53-10.55 Ma. Project 10.46 passes at all four wells. Legacy 10.6 fails at Glayzer-3, where NN9 is present below the pick. The recalibrated 10.55 sits on the edge, needing zero NN9 below the pick at Glayzer-3, where 50 m are observed.
contradictions.test: Confirm Glayzer-3 NN9 (2060-2110 MD) is in situ, not caved.

contradictions.finding: Imbok-1 'Top Stage IVA (Uncon.)' at 1303 MD lies inside a 580 m NN7 span (1090-1670 MD): window 10.89-11.90 Ma, and interpolation gives 11.26 Ma. Project 11.63 passes, legacy 12.0 fails, and recalibrated 11.90 sits on the edge. With one well this is a single witness only.
contradictions.test: Check the Imbok-1 ST-1 datum (shallow IVB/UIU picks conflict with NN10 and are excluded). Find a second NN6/NN7-bracketed LIU pick.

contradictions.finding: Both wells with picks (Gajah Hitam-1, Maligan-1) put Horizon III inside NN11 (5.59-8.29), so both models pass at zone level. Maligan-1 places it in NN11C-D (upper NN11), which favours the younger legacy 6.7 Ma. Also, 8.11 is not a GTS2012 zone boundary (base NN11 = 8.29); its source needs checking.
contradictions.test: Calibrate NN11 subzones (A-D) with the PETRONAS 2024 chart and re-read Horizon III at all NN11 wells.

contradictions.models: Base IVF: P 3.1 vs L ~5.5 | Base IVG: P 2.0 vs L 3.8
contradictions.finding: Offsets of 1.7-2.4 Ma are far too large to be calibration. The project scheme (Phase I p8: IVE = NN16-NN11) stretches IVE to ~5 Myr and compresses IVF-IVG into the last 3.1 Myr; the legacy scheme keeps IVF = NN12-NN16 and IVG from 3.8 Ma. These are two different stage definitions under the same names.
contradictions.test: Decide which definition is canonical before Phase II mapping. Then rename one set (e.g. IVE-P vs IVE-L) in all data.

contradictions.finding: The project equates Top II with BMU at 23.13; the legacy chart puts Base III at TB2.1 (~21). Possibly two surfaces of one Early Miocene event family (22-20 Ma deformation).
contradictions.test: Out of Phase I scope (NN8 and below deferred). Carry both.

contradictions.finding: 'SRU' is picked at top IVA (Deluar-1), base IVF (Ketam-1), base IVF/G (South Lokan-1), top IVC (Maligan-1) and base IVD (7 wells). 'DRU' is picked at base IVC at Tiga Papan-2 where NN5-NN8 is missing. On highs the names attach to whichever erosion surface is deepest.
contradictions.test: Tag such picks as composite (e.g. DRU+LIU+UIU) and exclude them from age calibration of the single surface.

contradictions.models: RU/MMU ~16 Ma (end of spreading) vs DRU 14.2-15.4
contradictions.finding: Copilot merges 'DRU/MMU'. They are different physics in different domains: rift-end drowning on the lower plate versus collision and inversion in the upper plate. They may be linked (end of spreading as continental crust jams the trench) and near-coeval, but are not one surface. Tiga Papan-2's '(MMU)' label shows the term has leaked inboard.
contradictions.test: Trace both on a dip keyline across the trough; look for onlap of trough fill onto DG drowned platforms vs DRU truncation inboard.

contradictions.models: pen chart: Kinarut = Stage IVC (H136, NN10) | Copilot v1.1 (citing Atlas Ch.5): Kinarut in Stage IVE
contradictions.finding: The Atlas chapter was not available to this build. Fan names are package names, not chronostratigraphic units.
contradictions.test: Read Atlas_Chapter 5 Sabah_v1.1; resolve before using fan names in GDE maps.

contradictions.finding: (a) Phase I p8 calls the NN9 Stage IVc horizon a 'mid-Miocene' unconformity; NN9 is early Tortonian (Late Miocene). (b) p8 places thrust-belt initiation in 'Bunguran and Baram'; Bunguran is Natuna (Indonesia). (c) The unified table labels Stage I 'Late Oligocene (Priabonian)'; Priabonian is Late Eocene. (d) The table labels IVA (top 11.63) 'Late Miocene (Tortonian)'; IVA is Langhian-Serravallian.

Kudat-1: '?Crocker Fm' at 2336-2475 MD carries NN9a nannofossils (formation call or caving issue). Maligan-1: ?NN10D above NN11D-C (reversal -> reworking). Imbok-1: shallow UIU/IVB picks above NN10. Rusa Timur-1: 'NN1' at 463-873 MD (truncated label).
contradictions.test: Raw occurrence charts + abundance to separate in-situ vs reworked (C3 of Copilot v0.1).

contradictions.models: Copilot: inboard deepwater shale until ~3 Ma; Stage IVA 'shallow-marine/deltaic'
contradictions.finding: Wells show both, but diachronously: Stage III is bathyal inboard (Deluar-1, Ketam-1, South Lokan-1); IVA is coastal on inversion highs but bathyal in the outer shelf (Rusa Timur-1, Gajah Hitam-1). The shelf edge then steps NW, reaching Rusa Timur at SRU time and Gajah Hitam in IVE. Shoaling is time-transgressive, not one horizontal facies switch.
contradictions.test: Plot EOD-vs-age for all 35+ biostrat wells to map shelf-edge trajectory.

contradictions.finding: Undeclared non-linear time axis; onshore Crocker drawn as Neogene depocentre (it was the eroding source); diapirs coloured as hiatus; unsourced volcanics; 'Base NN4' at 15.5 Ma (GTS2012 base NN4 = 17.95); stage blocks mix top- and base-of-stage conventions (e.g. 9.53-11.63 labelled IVC-IVB).

contradictions.topic: Cause of the post-16 Ma apparent-age signals
contradictions.models: A older magmatism + younger reworking (VIABLE, MED) | B polyphase magmatism (PLAUSIBLE, LOW-MED) | C apparent youth without new magma (VIABLE, MED)
contradictions.finding: Layang-Layang-1 gives young apparent ages (6.5-7.8 Ma, 13.6 Ma) interleaved with old ones (19.6-22.9 Ma) and no depth progression. Every young K-Ar result is either a low-radiogenic separate (5.0-5.2% 40Ar*) or a bulk sample; none is a primary-mineral crystallisation age. All three models fit the current data. Models A and C explain young apparent ages without a new magma pulse; Model B explains them by true younger emplacement. Bulk and fine-fraction K-Ar cannot separate them. No model is preferred.
contradictions.test: Promotion tests: (1) mineral-specific dating of screened primary igneous phases; (2) independent, well-tied cross-cutting seismic geometry.

contradictions.topic: Apparent age vs crystallisation / emplacement age
contradictions.models: K-Ar apparent age | crystallisation age | emplacement age
contradictions.finding: Aggregate K-Ar on >2 µm fractions and bulk samples mixes primary and secondary mineral domains. A K-Ar apparent age is a mixture age until the dated phase is shown to be primary and closed.
contradictions.test: No apparent age in this chart is labelled an emplacement age.

contradictions.models: in-situ intrusion AND/OR redeposited volcaniclastics, determined body by body
contradictions.finding: Volcanogenic sediment deposition and reworking are supported; possible in-situ dyke or sill geometries are interpreted (both reported by the enterprise validation dossier from the LL-1 post-drill study; not verified in the working folder). The present evidence does not show that every volcanic-looking seismic body has the same origin. Rule: classify each body independently.
contradictions.test: Per body: well-tied seismic geometry; contact petrography; chilled margin or baking; clast vs coherent groundmass texture; chemostratigraphic continuity; thermal alteration of host sediment; age relationship between body and host.

contradictions.models: local apparent ages | Mt Kinabalu granite 7.85-7.22 Ma | SCS spreading cessation 16-20 Ma (preliminary)
contradictions.finding: Regional Late Miocene magmatism (Mt Kinabalu) and post-spreading timing make a young local event plausible, but they are different domains and different plumbing. They are kept in a separate analogue ledger and never plotted as local evidence.
contradictions.test: Only local, mineral-specific ages promote Phase C (see confidence ladder).

phase_c.summary: Local apparent-age evidence exists; emplacement age unresolved.
phase_c.warning: Aggregate K-Ar measurements include mixed primary and secondary mineral domains. Apparent ages must not be treated as emplacement ages without petrographic separation and mineral-specific dating.
phase_c.depth_order_note: Depth order does not produce a simple age progression: 7.8, 6.5, 22.9, 7.3, 19.6, 13.6, 17.0 Ma from 4077 to 4293 m MD.

samples.treatment: MEDIUM; strongest local young apparent-age signal
MEDIUM apparent age; possible mixed or intermediate system

models.name: Model A — Older magmatism plus younger drape / reworking
models.description: The old K-Ar population (19.6-22.9 Ma), volcaniclastic deposition and younger fossil signals without any new magma.
models.falsifier: Replicated younger-than-16 Ma crystallisation ages from pristine primary minerals or chilled margins.

models.name: Model B — Genuine polyphase magmatism
models.description: An older Early Miocene system plus a discrete post-spreading pulse.
models.falsifier: Young ages occur only in secondary alteration phases and no young cross-cutting geometry exists.

models.name: Model C — Apparent youth without new magma
models.description: Alteration, partial isotopic resetting, hydrothermal circulation, redeposition or fault reactivation produce young signals.
models.falsifier: A concordant young crystallisation age from a pristine primary mineral, fresh groundmass, zircon or baddeleyite confirmed to be primary.

criteria: local apparent-age signals younger than 16 Ma

gate_med.criteria: EITHER concordant younger-than-16 Ma primary-mineral crystallisation ages from two screened in-situ samples OR one well-tied intrusion demonstrably younger than a secure post-16 Ma horizon

rules.inequality: age(body) > age(drape base) - body existed before the drape was deposited
age(intrusion) < age(crossed horizon) - intrusion is younger
age(deformation source) < age(youngest deformed package) - only if the causal link to the intrusion is demonstrated
separate intrusive levels; NOT automatically separate ages
age(body relief) >= age(oldest onlapping reflector) - write the inequality; onlap alone is not an age

rules: Long-ranging species are expressed as 'not older than', 'not younger than', 'and/or older' or 'and/or younger'.
No long-ranging occurrence is turned into a zonal top or absolute age without the raw occurrence chart and assemblage support.
Reworking, caving, barren samples, abundance and preservation controls are carried where available.
Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
biostratigraphic_discipline.encoding_status: PARTIAL - the v2 well windows use zone assignments as reported in the penetration chart. Raw occurrence charts, abundance, preservation and barren-sample flags are NOT encoded, so every window is a zone-level constraint, not a species-level age.

findings.title: Phase C is a candidate, not an event
findings.body: Layang-Layang-1 gives young apparent ages (6.5–7.8, 13.6 Ma) interleaved with old ones (19.6–22.9 Ma) and no depth progression. None is a primary-mineral crystallisation age. Models A, B and C all remain open (C15–C18).
